input.job: Open an issue in the user's repository when they report a bug to the agent

guide.job: Open an issue in the user's repository when they report a bug to the agent
guide.summary: To let your users connect their GitHub accounts to your agent, register a standard GitHub OAuth app, handle the web application flow to obtain access tokens, and use the GitHub REST API to create issues. Be aware that organization-level repositories may require organization owner approval due to default access restrictions.

verdict.difficulty_reason: Registering an OAuth app is completely self-serve with no review required by GitHub.
verdict.approval_wait: none for personal accounts; depends on organization owners for organization repositories

composio.note: Composio has a GitHub toolkit with 877 actions and managed auth as an alternative route.

route.name: Direct OAuth App
route.reason: You registered your own GitHub OAuth app to handle user authentication and tokens manually.

paths.name: Use Composio managed OAuth
paths.when_to_choose: If you want to skip manual OAuth app configuration and token handling.
paths.tradeoffs: Relies on a third-party managed auth layer rather than your own registered OAuth app.

paths.name: Personal Access Token Shortcut
paths.when_to_choose: For local testing or single-user proof of concepts.
paths.tradeoffs: Does not support multiple external users connecting their own accounts.

prerequisites.how_to_get: Sign up for a free account on the GitHub website.
prerequisites.done_when: You are logged into your GitHub dashboard

friction_checks.answer: Yes, registering an OAuth app is self-serve with no review.

friction_checks.check: Do organizations block OAuth apps by default?
friction_checks.answer: New organizations have OAuth app access restrictions enabled by default, requiring owner approval.
friction_checks.handled_in: Request organization owner approval if needed

steps.title: Register your GitHub OAuth application
actions: Go to **Developer settings** under your user settings
Click **OAuth apps** and then **New OAuth App**
Fill out application details and callback URL, then click **Register application**
steps.detail: Creating your own OAuth app gives you client credentials to start the web application flow for your users.
steps.done_when: You receive a Client ID and Client Secret for your application

steps.title: Configure environment variables securely
actions: Copy your **Client ID** and **Client Secret** into your local environment file
steps.detail: Your agent code requires these credentials to securely initiate the OAuth web application flow and exchange codes for tokens.
steps.done_when: Client ID and Client Secret are accessible in your backend configuration

steps.title: Implement OAuth web application flow
actions: Write code to redirect users to GitHub for authorization with requested scopes
Handle the callback redirect to exchange the temporary code for an access token via POST
steps.detail: Users must grant your app access so your agent can obtain a temporary code and trade it for an OAuth token.
steps.agent_prompt: Write the server endpoint using the GitHub web application flow to redirect users to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with client_id and scopes (repo, public_repo), and handle the callback at POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token to exchange the code for an access token.
steps.done_when: Your backend successfully receives and stores user access tokens

steps.title: Call REST API to create issues
actions: Implement the logic using the user's OAuth token to submit bug report data to the issues endpoint
steps.detail: Using the acquired token, your agent can make authenticated requests to open issues on the user's repository.
steps.agent_prompt: Write a function that takes a user's OAuth token, repository owner, repository name, title, and body, and sends a POST request to https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues with the Authorization Bearer header set.
steps.done_when: The agent can successfully create a GitHub issue programmatically

steps.title: Test end-to-end bug reporting flow
actions: Simulate a user bug report and verify that an issue is successfully opened in the target repository
steps.detail: Ensures that the entire pipeline from user sign-in to token handling and issue creation works correctly.
steps.done_when: An issue appears in the test repository matching the user's report

steps.title: Make your agent do the job
actions: Copy the prompt below into your coding agent.
Run it once with your own account.
steps.detail: This is the point of the prototype: your agent using the connection.
steps.done_when: Your agent completed the job in GitHub for your own account.
steps.agent_prompt: First check the connect step really happened: the GitHub tool exists and is registered with my agent.  If anything is missing, stop and tell me what. Otherwise run my agent once on this job with my own account: Open an issue in the user's repository when they report a bug to the agent. Show me what changed in GitHub.

glossary.plain: The URL to which GitHub redirects users after they authorize your application.

scopes.why: Provides full control of private and public repositories, necessary to create issues.
Grants access to read and write public repositories if full repo scope is not desired.

approval.process: New organizations have OAuth app access restrictions enabled by default, requiring an organization owner to approve the application before it can access organization resources.
approval.wait: Dependent on organization owner action; personal accounts require no review or wait.

blockers.mitigation: Request organization owner approval via the organization settings page.

alternatives: Use Composio managed authentication toolkit for GitHub

Make POST requests to the GitHub REST API to create issues
you_must_do: Register the OAuth application in developer settings
Configure client secrets in environment variables
Obtain organization owner approval if accessing organization repositories
guide.next_action: Register your GitHub OAuth application under your developer settings.
open_questions: Whether target repositories belong to restricted organizations requiring manual owner consent.
